chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: “There is no hadd punishment against one upon whom no hadd applies.”

Meaning: if an insane person were to falsely accuse a man, I do not consider anything to be upon him. And if a man were to accuse him and say to him, “O fornicator,” there would likewise be no hadd upon him.

key_terms.قَذَفَ: to accuse someone of illicit sexual conduct
key_terms.مَجْنُونًا: an insane person lacking legal responsibility

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment for slander apply when the accusation involves an insane person?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning slander and the hadd punishment: one who is not legally subject to hadd is not the basis for imposing hadd in return. The Imam عليه السلام illustrates this through the case of a majnun, indicating the absence of legal liability in such circumstances.
